title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. pi_{0,3}^ is the profinite fundamental group of P^1 minus {0,1,infinity}, free profinite on two generators. rho is the order-3 'rotation' automorphism that permutes the three standard loops cyclically. The 'équation des lacets' / 'équation en lambda' is the second (triangle/hexagon-type) Grothendieck–Teichmüller relation. Grothendieck writes it for xi = lambda rho(lambda)^{-1}, with an exponent gamma = (p-1)/2, where p in Z^x plays the role of the cyclotomic parameter (Drinfeld's lambda, with gamma his m). In Drinfeld's form it reads f(z,x) z^m f(y,z) y^m f(x,y) x^m = 1. It is a twisted 1-cocycle condition for Z/3 acting through rho. The next page accordingly opens a digression on 1-cocycles of cyclic groups: g rho(g) ... rho^{n-1}(g) = 1 characterises the splittings of pi x| Z/n.

Previous page. The equation is pushed down to the 'anodyne' quotient SL(2,Z^)'. This is a congruence-type image of pi_{0,3}^, a level-2 situation, which is why lambda_0 ≡ 1 mod 2. There the equation reduces to a quadratic-form condition on entries (c,d) of the matrix: D = c^2+cd+d^2 in Z^x (or the variant 3(c^2+cd)+d^2). Using surjectivity of the cyclotomic character, he checks prime by prime that every p in Z^x is of the form 1/D. For l ≠ 3 either form represents all units (and for l = 2 one may take c even, d odd). For l = 3 the form c^2+cd+d^2 gives exactly p ≡ 1 mod 3, and -3(c^2+cd)-d^2 gives exactly p ≡ -1 mod 3.

This page.
- He had hoped the abundance of solutions downstairs would yield a method to build large families ('gros paquets') of solutions in pi_{0,3}^.
- He admits complete failure: he cannot write down explicitly even one solution besides the trivial ones u = 1 and u = tau_infinity. These are the identity and complex-conjugation-type elements, with p = ±1.
- He then poses a lifting question. Take lambda_0 in SL(2,Z^)', lambda_0 ≡ 1 (2), such that xi_0 = lambda_0 rho(lambda_0)^{-1} satisfies the reduced equation for some gamma = (p-1)/2, i.e. c^2+cd+d^2 in Z^x (resp. the other form).
- Does there exist lambda in pi_{0,3}^ above lambda_0 such that xi = lambda rho(lambda)^{-1} satisfies the full equation, necessarily with the same gamma?
- In modern terms: is the image of (a rotation-equation analogue of) GT^ in its congruence/SL2 quotient everything permitted by the reduced equation? Equivalently, does every 'congruence-level' solution lift?
errors: No mathematical error on the page; it is a question. The arithmetic statements on the previous page about which units are represented by c^2+cd+d^2 and by -3(c^2+cd)-d^2 over Z_l (l = 3 versus l ≠ 3) are correct.

The gamma-dependence is somewhat loose. Downstairs the condition 'D in Z^x' does not by itself pin p (p relates to 1/D), and the parenthetical alternative xi = lambda(...)rho(lambda_0)^{-1} is garbled. Which normalisation of xi he intends is unclear.

ideas.what: Rotation form of the GT 'triangle/hexagon' relation written as a twisted cocycle equation xi = lambda rho(lambda)^{-1} for the order-3 automorphism rho of pi_{0,3}^, with exponent (p-1)/2
ideas.modern_name: Grothendieck–Teichmüller relation (II) / hexagon relation for GT^
ideas.usually_credited_to: Drinfeld (1990); Ihara; Grothendieck's Esquisse (1984) as programme
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme sketches the GT idea; this explicit equation is in the Longue Marche follow-up notes (unpublished)

ideas.what: Reduction of the equation to the congruence image in SL(2,Z^)', where it becomes a condition that a binary quadratic form c^2+cd+d^2 take unit values, checked prime by prime
ideas.modern_name: Image of GT^ / Galois in congruence quotients (level-2 / SL2 image)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Ihara, Nakamura, Lochak–Schneps (studies of GT and modular/congruence quotients)

ideas.what: Admission that no explicit nontrivial solution (other than identity and complex conjugation) can be constructed
ideas.modern_name: Non-constructibility of explicit elements of GT^ beyond ±1
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore; noted repeatedly in the GT literature since Drinfeld/Ihara

ideas.what: Lifting question: does every congruence-level solution lambda_0 lift to a solution in pi_{0,3}^ with the same gamma?
ideas.modern_name: Surjectivity of GT^ (or of its rotation-equation analogue) onto its admissible congruence-level image
ideas.usually_credited_to: Related questions studied by Nakamura, Lochak–Schneps, Hoshi–Minamide–Mochizuki (unsure exact formulation)

missed.claim: Grothendieck formulates a lifting problem for the loop/rotation equation: given a solution in the congruence quotient SL(2,Z^)' (lambda_0 ≡ 1 mod 2, satisfying the quadratic-form unit condition), does there exist a lift lambda in pi_{0,3}^ satisfying the full equation with the same cyclotomic exponent? He leaves it open.
missed.quote: Existe-t-il donc un ξ∈π̂_{0,3} au-dessus de λ_0, tel que ξ=λρ(λ)^{-1} (resp. ...) satisfasse aussi une équation en ξ (nécessairement avec le même γ)?
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It is a concrete approximation-type question about the image of GT^ (or its rotation analogue) in congruence quotients. It bears on how far GT^ is from Gal(Q-bar/Q). Comparable lifting/image questions appear in work on GT and modular towers, but this exact formulation via the level-2 SL2 quotient and the form c^2+cd+d^2 does not appear to be recorded.

deep.surprise_reason: The page contains a clearly posed open lifting question, plus an honest admission that no explicit nontrivial solution can be built. The admission matches what the GT community independently knows. The specific SL2/quadratic-form reduction and lifting formulation is an unpublished detail, but related image/lifting questions for GT^ have been studied, so it is not startling.
transcription_corrections: Line 1: 'tenir une méthode pour construire ≃ dans' is likely '[ob]tenir une méthode pour construire ainsi dans'; '≃' is the abbreviation for 'ainsi'.
'pas = d'en construire' should read 'pas même d'en construire'.
'Existe-t-il dans un ξ' should read 'Existe-t-il donc un ξ'.
'(resp. 3(c²+cd)+d² ∈ Ẑ^×)' follows 'c²+d²+cd ∈ Ẑ^×'; the handwriting looks like 'resp.' / 'res.', consistent with the previous page.

The parenthetical 'ξ=λ(-l_0^{-1})ρ(λ_0)^{-1}' is uncertain; it appears to be an alternative normalisation of ξ_0 in terms of λ_0 (e.g. λ_0^{-1}... ρ(λ_0)^{-1}), followed by the struck-out 'soit tel que'.
'u=τ_∞' is correct as read; it denotes the complex-conjugation-type trivial solution.
